title: Bellevue Live! Pass — Evidence register
scope: Targeted design and feasibility review; not a systematic literature review.
integrity: No private heatmaps, conversion funnels, click maps or participant results were obtained. Official product descriptions are observational evidence of advertised capabilities. Design implications are project inferences.

sources.title: My Disney Experience mobile app
sources.author: Walt Disney World Resort
sources.finding: The official app brings plans, tickets, dining, navigation and personalized itinerary assistance together.
sources.limitations: Feature marketing establishes advertised capability, not independently measured task success or conversion.
sources.designImplication: Keep tickets and reservations together; offer assistance within the journey.
sources.apa: Walt Disney World Resort. (n.d.). My Disney Experience mobile app.

sources.title: The official Universal Orlando app
sources.author: Universal Orlando Resort
sources.finding: Universal describes a ticket wallet, travel party, dining reservations, mobile ordering, maps and virtual assistance.
sources.limitations: Availability is selective; feature descriptions do not prove usability, economic uplift or applicability to Bellevue.
sources.designImplication: Provide group planning and useful in-venue actions, with supplier-specific availability.
sources.apa: Universal Orlando Resort. (n.d.). The official Universal Orlando app.

sources.title: Ticketmaster rolls out All In Prices as the global standard; outlines improvements to the ticketing experience
sources.author: Ticketmaster
sources.finding: Ticketmaster announced US upfront ticket prices including fees before taxes.
sources.limitations: Corporate announcement; it is not a causal study and excludes taxes from its stated upfront price.
sources.designImplication: Show a total early, itemize mandatory charges and label estimated costs.
sources.apa: Ticketmaster. (2025, May 12). Ticketmaster rolls out All In Prices as the global standard; outlines improvements to the ticketing experience.

sources.title: Season Ticket Family mobile ordering guide
sources.author: Chase Center
sources.finding: The arena guide connects mobile food ordering with ticket management and event discovery.
sources.limitations: Search-indexed official text was accessible; full dynamic page content was not. No measured efficiency claim is adopted.
sources.designImplication: Place food services beside active tickets, with clearly stated service eligibility.
sources.apa: Chase Center. (n.d.). Season Ticket Family mobile ordering guide.

sources.title: MGM Rewards mobile app
sources.author: MGM Resorts International
sources.finding: MGM describes mobile check-in, digital room keys at participating properties, dining reservations and show booking.
sources.limitations: Capabilities depend on property and eligibility; these are product descriptions, not evidence of Bellevue integrations.
sources.designImplication: Unify reservation visibility but preserve provider conditions and support.
sources.apa: MGM Resorts International. (n.d.). MGM Rewards mobile app.

sources.title: BelRed Station
sources.author: Sound Transit
sources.finding: BelRed is served by the 2 Line; both listed platforms are marked accessible. The page carries current arrivals and service alerts.
sources.limitations: Station accessibility does not verify a future venue walking route. Alerts are time-sensitive.
sources.designImplication: Link to the authoritative station page and mark proposed walking legs as illustrative.
sources.apa: Sound Transit. (n.d.-a). BelRed Station.

sources.title: Fares
sources.author: Sound Transit
sources.finding: Link 1/2 adult fares are $3 one way; youth 18 and under travel free; eligible reduced fares are $1. ORCA/contactless transfer credit applies within two hours.
sources.limitations: Snapshot retrieved 13 October 2026; eligibility and fare products require agency validation. This platform has no fare-sale agreement.
sources.designImplication: Calculate illustrative rail costs by rider type; explain that a demo bundle is not a valid transit pass.
sources.apa: Sound Transit. (n.d.-b). Fares.

sources.title: Link light rail opens across Lake Washington
sources.author: Sound Transit
sources.finding: The Crosslake Connection opened on 28 March 2026, joining the 2 Line with the regional network.
sources.limitations: Opening-day service descriptions are not a current timetable and do not establish a direct rail service to Tulalip.
sources.designImplication: Represent Bellevue rail access and the onward Tulalip road connection as separate legs.
sources.apa: Sound Transit. (2026, March 28). Link light rail opens across Lake Washington.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.author: World Wide Web Consortium
sources.finding: WCAG 2.2 specifies testable accessibility success criteria, including keyboard operation, contrast, focus and target-size requirements.
sources.limitations: Meeting selected checks does not establish full conformance; evaluation must include content, complete processes and assistive technology.
sources.designImplication: Use WCAG 2.2 AA as a verification target with human testing.
sources.apa: World Wide Web Consortium. (2024, December 12). Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2.

sources.title: Understanding navigation
sources.author: Google Material Design
sources.finding: Material guidance places three to five top-level destinations in a mobile bottom navigation bar.
sources.limitations: Guidance is not a study proving the optimal labels or order for this particular platform.
sources.designImplication: Retain five named destinations and test their interpretation.
sources.apa: Google. (n.d.). Understanding navigation. Material Design.

sources.title: Hamburger menus and hidden navigation hurt UX metrics
sources.author: Kara Pernice and Raluca Budiu
sources.finding: A study with 179 participants on six sites found hidden navigation less discoverable than visible or combined navigation.
sources.limitations: The mobile study compared hidden with combined navigation, not every visible-navigation variant. Sites and devices differ from this prototype.
sources.designImplication: Keep core journeys visible; reserve the account menu for secondary functions.
sources.apa: Pernice, K., & Budiu, R. (2016, June 26). Hamburger menus and hidden navigation hurt UX metrics. Nielsen Norman Group.

sources.title: Checkout optimization: 5 ways to minimize form fields in checkout
sources.author: Edward Scott
sources.finding: Baymard's checkout research emphasizes the burden of form fields over simply counting checkout steps.
sources.limitations: General ecommerce evidence; the public article does not expose all raw data, and travel bookings require different information.
sources.designImplication: Keep ticket-only checkout short, reuse party details and disclose optional additions progressively.
sources.apa: Scott, E. (2024, June 26). Checkout optimization: 5 ways to minimize form fields in checkout. Baymard Institute.

sources.title: Smart tourism: foundations and developments
sources.author: Ulrike Gretzel, Marianna Sigala, Zheng Xiang and Chulmo Koo
sources.finding: Smart tourism connects destination infrastructure, information, businesses and visitor experience; an app alone is insufficient.
sources.limitations: Conceptual position paper, not an experimental estimate of visitation effects.
sources.designImplication: Evaluate movement and partner outcomes as well as interface engagement.
sources.apa: Gretzel, U., Sigala, M., Xiang, Z., & Koo, C. (2015). Smart tourism: Foundations and developments. Electronic Markets, 25, 179–188. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12525-015-0196-8

sources.title: Evolving to a new dominant logic for marketing
sources.author: Stephen L. Vargo and Robert F. Lusch
sources.finding: The paper frames exchange around service, relationships and the co-creation of value.
sources.limitations: Broad marketing theory does not establish this platform's market fit or commercial viability.
sources.designImplication: Treat visitors and destination operators as participants in service delivery.
sources.apa: Vargo, S. L., & Lusch, R. F. (2004). Evolving to a new dominant logic for marketing. Journal of Marketing, 68(1), 1–17. https://doi.org/10.1509/jmkg.68.1.1.24036

sources.title: Understanding customer experience throughout the customer journey
sources.author: Katherine N. Lemon and Peter C. Verhoef
sources.finding: Customer experience extends across stages, channels and touchpoints involving multiple partners.
sources.limitations: Integrative framework rather than a trial of a dual-destination product.
sources.designImplication: Design service recovery and post-visit rewards alongside purchase.
sources.apa: Lemon, K. N., & Verhoef, P. C. (2016). Understanding customer experience throughout the customer journey. Journal of Marketing, 80(6), 69–96. https://doi.org/10.1509/jm.15.0420

sources.title: Welcome to the experience economy
sources.author: B. Joseph Pine II and James H. Gilmore
sources.finding: Memorable experiences form a distinct economic offering.
sources.limitations: Conceptual framing, not causal evidence.
sources.designImplication: Assess the whole visit.
sources.apa: Pine, B. J., II, & Gilmore, J. H. (1998). Welcome to the experience economy. Harvard Business Review, 76(4), 97–105.

sources.title: The goal-gradient hypothesis resurrected: Purchase acceleration, illusionary goal progress, and customer retention
sources.author: Ran Kivetz, Oleg Urminsky and Yuhuang Zheng
sources.finding: Field and experimental work links proximity to a reward goal with greater effort or purchase acceleration.
sources.limitations: Consumer reward contexts differ from high-cost arena visits. Effect sizes cannot be transferred to this proposal.
sources.designImplication: Show truthful earned progress; test comprehension and avoid fabricated head starts.
sources.apa: Kivetz, R., Urminsky, O., & Zheng, Y. (2006). The goal-gradient hypothesis resurrected: Purchase acceleration, illusionary goal progress, and customer retention. Journal of Marketing Research, 43(1), 39–58.

sources.title: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
sources.author: Stephanie Russo Carroll and colleagues
sources.finding: CARE addresses Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility and Ethics for Indigenous data.
sources.limitations: A general framework cannot substitute for nation-specific authority, consultation or agreements.
sources.designImplication: Give tribal partners authority over cultural content and collective data uses.
sources.apa: Carroll, S. R., Garba, I., Figueroa-Rodríguez, O. L., Holbrook, J., Lovett, R., Materechera, S., Parsons, M., Raseroka, K., Rodriguez-Lonebear, D., Rowe, R., Sara, R., Walker, J. D., Anderson, J., & Hudson, M. (2020). The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance. Data Science Journal, 19, Article 43. https://doi.org/10.5334/dsj-2020-043

sources.title: Who we are
sources.author: The Tulalip Tribes
sources.finding: The Tulalip Tribes describes its community and tribal sovereignty.
sources.limitations: The source establishes identity and context, not approval of the Bellevue Live proposal.
sources.designImplication: Use nation-specific attribution and separately negotiated participation.
sources.apa: The Tulalip Tribes. (n.d.). Who we are.

sources.title: League Pass blackout guide
sources.author: NBA Help Center
sources.finding: League Pass viewing is subject to geographic and broadcast restrictions.
sources.limitations: Consumer subscription rules do not grant a third-party arena app replay or distribution rights.
sources.designImplication: Treat live video as a separate licensed integration and demonstrate synthetic content.
sources.apa: NBA Help Center. (n.d.). League Pass blackout guide.

sources.title: Destination competitiveness: Determinants and indicators
sources.author: Larry Dwyer and Chulwon Kim
sources.finding: The model combines subjective and objective destination indicators and links competitiveness to socioeconomic prosperity.
sources.limitations: Institutional abstract and bibliographic record reviewed; not a Bellevue-specific estimate.
sources.designImplication: Include local business participation and community benefit in pilot evaluation.
sources.apa: Dwyer, L., & Kim, C. (2003). Destination competitiveness: Determinants and indicators. Current Issues in Tourism, 6(5), 369–414. https://doi.org/10.1080/13683500308667962

sources.title: Live Nation At The Concert
sources.author: Live Nation Worldwide, Inc.
sources.finding: The developer lists ticket purchase, mobile entry, offline ticket viewing, ordering and ticket transfer at participating venues.
sources.limitations: Developer claims describe capabilities; app-store reviews and ratings are not used as representative usability evidence.
sources.designImplication: Make saved demonstration plans available offline and distinguish ticket access from purchase.
sources.apa: Live Nation Worldwide, Inc. (2026, September 24). Live Nation At The Concert [Mobile app]. Google Play.
